A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable versions of the same UnMix-NeRF work, with matching sections, 16 equations, five figures and four tables. Both end with references and contain no appendices; the supplementary material mentioned in both is not included in the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original component ablations, hyperspectral reconstruction experiments on three datasets, and material-segmentation results, including F1 of 0.41 and mIoU of 0.28.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes in Section 5, Tables 1-4 and the qualitative figures.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same endmember dictionary, abundance and scaling heads, specular field, volumetric rendering, segmentation cluster probe and joint hyperspectral/RGB loss. Wording corrections do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both report the same NeSpoF, BaySpec and Surface Optics coverage, with unchanged scenes and spectral ranges. Hyperspectral view synthesis, material segmentation and scene-editing demonstrations are retained without an added task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains HS-NeRF and NeSpoF. Tables 3-4 retain NeRF, MipNeRF, TensoRF, Nerfacto, MipNeRF360, HS-NeRF, 3DGS and HyperGS. The newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged, including NeSpoF's S0-only evaluation, camera-pose usage, spectral coverage, evaluation metrics and 20,000 training iterations. Adding a citation for SAM in Section 5.1 does not change the metric or protocol.

E4.justification: Table 1 retains the same sequential ablation of physical constraints, scaling factors, RGB loss, VCA initialization and the specular field. The reconstruction-error, abundance, segmentation and editing examples are also unchanged; Figure 4 is only relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Table 2's averages remain averages across scenes rather than repeated trials.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1-4 and the qualitative result images are retained. Examples include NeSpoF average PSNR of 33.2 with 44-minute training, Caladium PSNR of 30.08, and segmentation F1/mIoU of 0.41/0.28. No numerical correction or new result is reported.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(16), the linear mixing assumptions, abundance constraints, rendering definitions and loss formulations are unchanged. No mathematical derivation, proposition or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating spectral unmixing with NeRF, joint synthesis and unsupervised material segmentation, material-based editing and superior performance. Reformatting the contribution list does not change its meaning.

C2.justification: The explanations of component effects in Section 5.2 and interpretations of reconstruction and segmentation results remain unchanged. No substantive limitation, failure condition or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v2 removes the acknowledgment identifying IBEX at KAUST as the computational-resource provider. This slightly reduces resource provenance; Section 4.6's hardware, memory, optimization and training settings, reported timings, and project-page information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Correa et al. (2017), Hinojosa et al. (2021) and Huang et al. (2022) to the spectral-imaging background, plus Kruse et al. (1993) for SAM. Existing references are retained, and novelty claims and positioning against prior methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar, punctuation and citation-spacing corrections, including 'constraint' to 'constrain' and correcting the loss-function discussion. It also numbers the contributions (i)-(iii) and rewrites the acknowledgment, while retaining the section organization and narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 4 and its caption move upward within page 7, preceding the continuation of the qualitative-results paragraph. There is minor caption punctuation and text/reference reflow, but all figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Grammar corrections and explicit sources for spectral imaging and SAM modestly improve readability and attribution. Scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged. Removing the IBEX acknowledgment slightly reduces resource provenance, but detailed hardware and training information remains, making the net improvement limited.
